title: Join now or stay stuck
passage: Summer is six weeks away. You can keep making excuses on the couch, or you can sign up for Brightrock's 6-Week Shred today and finally see results. There's no in-between. First week free for new members, and our coaches are ready when you are.
cue: keep making excuses on the couch, or you can sign up for Brightrock's 6-Week Shred
explanation: You could run, take a class somewhere else, or train at home. The ad pretends the only alternative to its program is sitting on the couch.

whyNot.fal_loaded_question: The ad doesn't hide an assumption inside a question; it openly offers two options as if nothing else exists.

source: Principal Gail Okafor · Spring family night
passage: Thank you all for coming out tonight. I know the budget is on everyone's mind, so here's where we are: either families accept the new $150 activity fee, or we cut music, art and sports next year. Those are the only two paths. Please share your thoughts at Tuesday's board meeting.
cue: either families accept the new $150 activity fee, or we cut music, art and sports
explanation: A school can also trim other costs, phase in a smaller fee, or look for grants. Principal Okafor presents two options as if nothing else were possible.

whyNot.fal_middle_ground: She isn't claiming a compromise must be right; she's hiding the compromises and alternatives that exist.

passage:
Noor: The cabin is $1,400 for the weekend, which is a lot. The campground is $90.
Eli: I checked the forecast too, and it might rain on Saturday.
Noor: So either we pay for the cabin or we spend two days soaked in a tent. Easy call.
cue: either we pay for the cabin or we spend two days soaked in a tent
explanation: The group could find a cheaper cabin, move the dates or bring a rain tarp. Noor shrinks a range of options down to $1,400 or misery.

whyNot.fal_loaded_question: Noor isn't asking a question with a hidden assumption; she's squeezing the choices down to two.

passage: Hot take after ten years in software: AI coding assistants are either going to replace every junior developer or they're useless autocomplete. I've used them daily for a year, and they're clearly not useless. So plan accordingly, juniors.
cue: either going to replace every junior developer or they're useless autocomplete
explanation: The tools could be genuinely useful without replacing anyone. Devon offers only two extremes, rules one out and treats the other as proven.

whyNot.fal_middle_ground: Devon isn't settling on a compromise; he skips the in-between possibilities entirely.

title: Pool resurfacing decision
passage: Dear residents, the inspector found cracks in the pool's plaster. We can approve the $62,000 full resurfacing this spring, or we can accept that the pool may need to close for good within a few years. Patching has already been tried twice. Please send us your preference by March 3.
cue: or we can accept that the pool may need to close for good
explanation: Residents might get other bids, phase the work or try a partial repair. The board frames one $62,000 job as the only alternative to losing the pool.

whyNot.fal_loaded_question: The board isn't hiding a disputed assumption in a question; it narrows a real decision down to two options.

title: Pick a lane, Fennel & Fig
passage: The new fall menu at Fennel & Fig adds six vegan dishes and drops four classics, including the lasagna. A restaurant either knows what it is or it chases trends, and this menu tells me which one they've picked. The squash risotto was lovely, to be fair, but I miss the old Fennel & Fig.
cue: A restaurant either knows what it is or it chases trends
explanation: A restaurant can keep its identity while trying new dishes. Tamsin assumes there are only two kinds of restaurant, then files Fennel & Fig under the bad one.

whyNot.fal_middle_ground: Tamsin isn't arguing for a compromise; she's ruling out the possibility of one.

passage:
Kai: There are only two trains to the airport before our flight: 11:40 tonight or 5:15 tomorrow morning.
Rosa: The 5:15 gets in at 6:05, and boarding closes at 6:00. So if we're going by train, it has to be the 11:40 tonight.
cue: if we're going by train, it has to be the 11:40 tonight
explanation: Rosa has checked the timetable: there really are only two trains, and one arrives too late. Narrowing to two options is fair when those are the only ones.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: The two choices really are the only trains, and Rosa shows why one fails. No reasonable option is being left out.

source: Engineer Tomas Varga · Millbrook water board
passage: We studied four ways to meet the new lead limits: treatment upgrades, pipe replacement, buying water from Fairview, or doing nothing. Fairview declined, and doing nothing isn't legal. That leaves two real options, and the cost tables in your packet compare them side by side.
cue: Fairview declined, and doing nothing isn't legal
explanation: Tomas started with four options and explains why two of them are off the table. Ending with two choices is fair when the others have been ruled out for stated reasons.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: He doesn't pretend only two options ever existed. He lists four and gives a reason for eliminating each of the other two.
